Proposition
[late-time standard solution modeled by ancient solutions] Source: cao-zhu 1. Assertion 1\group Ricci Flow with Surgery

For any $\varepsilon >0$, there is a positive number $\theta =\theta (\varepsilon )$ with $0<\theta <1$ such that for any $(x_0,t_0)\in \mathbb {R}^3\times [\theta ,1)$, the standard solution on the parabolic neighborhood $B_{t_0}(x,\varepsilon ^{-1}R(x_0,t_0)^{-\frac{1}{2}}) \times [t_0-\varepsilon ^{-2}R(x_0,t_0)^{-1},t_0]$ is well-defined and is, after scaling with the factor $R(x_0,t_0)$, $\varepsilon $-close (in the $C^{[\varepsilon ^{-1}]}$ topology) to the corresponding subset of some orientable ancient $\kappa $-solution.
